question: P, Q and R are the three angles of a triangle. If P - Q = 20∘ and Q - R = 26∘ , then ∠P is equal to:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Express all angles in terms of P to solve directly.

Q = P − 20° and R = Q − 26° ⇒ R = P − 46°

Sum of angles: P + (P − 20°) + (P − 46°) = 180°

3P − 66° = 180° ⇒ 3P = 246° ⇒ P = 82°

**∴ The correct answer is 82°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

⇒ P − Q = 20°

⇒ Q − R = 26°

**Formula Used:**

The sum of all interior angles in a triangle is 180°.

⇒ P + Q + R = 180°

 

 

 

 

 P
 Q
 R
 P = ?
 P − 20°
 P − 46°

**Calculations:**

⇒ From the first equation, Q = P − 20°

⇒ From the second equation, R = Q − 26°

⇒ Substitute Q into the R equation: R = (P − 20°) − 26° = P − 46°

⇒ Sum of the angles: P + (P − 20°) + (P − 46°) = 180°

⇒ 3P − 66° = 180°

⇒ 3P = 246°

⇒ P = 246° ÷ 3 = 82°

**∴ The correct answer is 82°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Angle Sum Property of a Triangle

The sum of all interior angles of a triangle is always equal to 180°. For any triangle ABC, ∠A + ∠B + ∠C = 180°.

Exterior Angle Theorem

The measure of an exterior angle of a triangle is equal to the sum of the measures of its two remote interior angles.

Classification by Angles

Triangles are classified into Acute (all angles 90°).
